What Is Corporate America Really Costing Black Men?

In this episode of A Black Executive Perspective Podcast, Tony Tidbit is joined by Justin Grant, author of Company Men: A Wellness Guide for Black Men in Corporate America, for a deep, unfiltered conversation about survival, strategy, and sustainability for Black men navigating corporate America.

Justin breaks down the hidden costs of success, why Black men experience increased anxiety and health risks as they rise professionally, and how corporate environments often reward proximity to power over performance alone. This conversation goes beyond motivation and dives into the real systems shaping opportunity, advancement, and burnout.

Together, Tony and Justin explore the difference between mentorship and sponsorship, why networking must be intentional rather than transactional, and how long-term career planning requires playing chess, not chasing titles. title: What Is Corporate America Really Costing Black Men?

Chris Casey: Markets Could See The Tariff Rollback Two Ways #tariffs #tariffnews #finance #markets

In this short clip, Chris Casey explains why markets may interpret a tariff rollback in two very different ways. On one hand, rescinding tariffs returns billions of dollars to the private sector — something free-market economists argue supports business investment and economic growth. On the other hand, with U.S. budget deficits running near $2 trillion annually, losing roughly $300 billion in tariff revenue could raise fresh concerns about fiscal solvency and government debt sustainability.

TRUMP JUST PROVED DEI WORKS

When President Biden nominated Ketanji Brown Jackson, many critics screamed “DEI hire” despite her elite résumé and top-tier judicial experience. In this video, I break down why Trump’s recent pick of Dr. Erica Schwartz for a top public health role actually shows how DEI is supposed to work: it doesn’t replace merit, it expands the pool so true merit can finally be seen.

We walk through Ketanji Brown Jackson’s credentials, compare them to Trump’s loyalty pick of Markwayne Mullin for DHS, and then show why going outside Trump’s usual inner circle to consider a broader, more diverse slate of candidates led him to a deeply qualified choice in Dr. Schwartz. This is what happens when you stop hiring only from the same homogenous network and start looking across all of Main Street.
